races.paceDynamic: With Lethal Blast non-running, this race loses its confirmed front runner and becomes a messy pace puzzle. Poetic Jack is the only prominent runner left, but may face early company from hold-up horses pushed into unnatural positions. The likely result is a moderate early pace that could quicken suddenly when multiple hold-up horses make their moves simultaneously in the final two furlongs. This tactical scenario strongly favours horses with proven finishing kicks who can respond when the race develops late - the hold-up specialists with good turn of foot will have the edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays moderate and multiple closers finish strongly
scenarios.body: The abundance of hold-up runners creates a tactical finish where those with the best acceleration thrive. Horses like Southbank and Elvetham, both proven finishers, can capitalise on their preferred running style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Poetic Jack Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Poetic Jack gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: The Robert Cowell-trained runner under Hollie Doyle can use tactical speed to steal a march on the field. His prominent style becomes a major advantage when he's not pressured for the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Early Positioning
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses are pushed out of their comfort zones early
scenarios.body: The lack of natural pace-setters creates awkward positioning and a stop-start rhythm that suits adaptable types. Horses with versatile running styles can exploit the tactical confusion better than one-dimensional closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Materialises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a dash from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes purely about raw finishing speed rather than tactical positioning. This extreme scenario would favour horses with the highest closing gears regardless of their usual running style.

races.paceDynamic: Lion Ring stands alone as the confirmed front-runner and will dictate a measured pace from the off, with Alashos and Porfin likely to track just behind in prominent positions. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Lion Ring can control fractions without being harassed early, creating a tactical tempo rather than a searching gallop. This sets up perfectly for the prominent runners who can stay close without expending energy, while the large contingent of hold-up horses will need the pace to collapse late to make their moves count. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can stay handy and kick when Lion Ring's stamina gives out.

scenarios.label: A

scenarios.trigger: If Lion Ring sets steady fractions and Alashos or Porfin can track without pressure
scenarios.body: The prominent pair stay within striking distance as Lion Ring's 8-year-old legs tire, allowing them to pounce in the final furlong when the hold-up brigade have too much ground to make up. Fresh legs and tactical positioning prove decisive over raw finishing speed.

scenarios.body: The crawling tempo plays into the hands of a classy closer who can unleash a devastating late run when others have gone too early. Superior class and finishing kick overcomes poor positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lion Ring Wire Special
scenarios.trigger: If Lion Ring's recent course form and tactical advantage prove too much
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old uses his 10-day turnaround and proven 6f speed to steal a march when others expect him to fold, grinding out victory through sheer bloody-mindedness. Experience trumps youth in a tactical finish.

races.paceDynamic: Dalmally represents the only confirmed front runner in this field, meaning he can dictate terms without early pressure and set a measured, sustainable pace through the opening half-mile. The lack of pace rivals allows him to control splits and save energy for the finish, while the massive field of hold-up horses will bunch together in behind, creating a compact pack that must rely on late pace. This tactical setup heavily favours horses with early pace positioning - either Dalmally himself or any runner comfortable sitting prominent - as they avoid the traffic and trouble that awaits the crowded hold-up brigade. The race shape strongly benefits front runners and prominent racers who can track the lone pace setter.

scenarios.label: A

scenarios.trigger: If Dalmally breaks cleanly and faces no early challengers for the lead
scenarios.body: His uncontested fractions allow him to dictate ideal splits and kick clear when the field comes hunting. The hold-up horses face a wall of traffic trying to get through the packed field behind him.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.trigger: If one of the better hold-up horses manages to secure an early prominent position behind Dalmally
scenarios.body: They get first run on the leader while avoiding the traffic nightmare developing behind them. The tactical advantage of a clear passage proves decisive over superior but trapped rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes overly strong or Dalmally stops quickly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The superior class horses from deep can unleash powerful finishing kicks to overhaul the pace advantage. Mr Fustic and Secret Road have the form figures to suggest they can produce big efforts when the pace sets up right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic-Troubled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches tightly turning for home with multiple horses looking for racing room
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery of who finds the clearest passage rather than who has the best finishing kick. Riders' positioning skills and horse's ability to quicken in tight quarters become crucial.
